messages.subject: Make shinyapps.io user guide repo public so users can submit pull requests?

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

While reading more about application tuning in the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> user guide (http://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/), I noticed a broken link [to what I presume to be a since-renamed section]. I know the user guide, which is fantastic btw, has been updated fairly recently, so I imagine catching this sort of thing is only a matter of time, but it seems like an easy fix would be to make the repo publicly available and allow users to submit pull requests. The alternatives–creating an entire thread on here or emailing support seem like overkill for minor edits–but I would happily commit the free labor if it's convenient while I'm working through the documentation anyway.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Shiny: Help Defining a Custom SliderInput Step set
messages.subject_clean: Shiny: Help Defining a Custom SliderInput Step set
messages.body_plain:
Hi Guys,

I have integrated Shiny with Leaflet, with a working SliderInput. The problem is that there are a lot of values at the lower part of the Sliderinput scale and very few values towards the upper part of the scale.

I have tried using steps of 50 which doesn't seem to work and I would ideally like to go up in steps of (10, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 4000) on the slider bar.

I am asking for help on defining a custom Slider input, with the above steps.

I would be most thankful if someone could help solve this issue,

Kind regards,
Tom.

############################################################
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
library(leaflet)
library(rgdal)
library(sp)
library(rsconnect)

crime <- readOGR("./crime2017a",layer="crime2017a")
crime <- spTransform(crime, CRS("+init=epsg:4326"))
names(crime) <- c("LSOA","Crime_count","Anti_social_behaviour","Burglary","Violent_crime","Shoplifting","Criminal_damage")

#custom tiles
MBaccessToken <- "X" #removed
MBurlTemplate <- "X=" #removed
MBTemplate <- paste(MBurlTemplate,MBaccessToken,sep="")

ui <- dashboardPage(skin="black",
                    dashboardHeader(title = "Crime Reported in Liverpool 2017", titleWidth = 450),
                    dashboardSidebar(width = 450,
                                     tags$head(
                                       tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css", href = "custom.css"),
                                       tags$script(src = "custom.js")
                                     ),
                                     sidebarMenu(
                                       menuItem("Maps", tabName = "maps", icon = icon("globe")),
                                       menuItem("Charts", icon = icon("map"), tabName = "charts"))
                    ),

                    dashboardBody(
                      sliderInput("range", "Crime Count", min(crime$Crime_count), max(crime$Crime_count),
                                  value = range(crime$Crime_count), step = 50),
                      # Also add some custom CSS to make the title background area the same
                      # color as the rest of the header.
                      tags$head(tags$style(HTML('
                                                .skin-blue .main-header .logo {
                                                background-color: #3c8dbc;
                                                }
                                                .skin-blue .main-header .logo:hover {
                                                background-color: #3c8dbc;
                                                }
                                                '))),

                      leafletOutput("mymap",width="100%",height="1000px"),
                      tabItems(
                        tabItem(tabName = "maps"),

                        tabItem(tabName = "charts")
                      )
                      )
                      )

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  #set slider ranges
  filteredData <- reactive({
    crime[crime$Crime_count >= input$range[1] & crime$Crime_count<= input$range[2],]
  }) #range[1] = min #range[2]= max

  colorpal <- reactive({
    pal <- colorQuantile("YlOrRd", domain = crime$Crime_count, n=8)
  })

  output$mymap <- renderLeaflet({

    #reactive expression represents the palette function,
    # which changes as the user makes selections in UI.

    leaflet(crime) %>%
      addTiles(MBTemplate, options=tileOptions(minZoom=11, maxZoom=18)) %>%
      setView(-2.959761, 53.404049, 11)

  })

  #only elements that are reactive are defined here
  observe({
    pal <- colorpal()

    leafletProxy("mymap", data = filteredData())  %>%
      clearShapes() %>%
      addPolygons(
        fillColor = ~pal(Crime_count),
        fillOpacity = 0.6,
        popup = ~paste(Crime_count),
        color = "#BDBDC3",
        weight = 1)
  })

  observe({
    proxy <- leafletProxy("mymap", data = crime)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
############################################################

messages.body_plain:
I have an app (peppro.org <http://peppro.org>) that generates a pdf report after the user has analysed his/her data. knit2pdf() works fine in my laptop but I can't get it to work as long as when I upload it to the shinyapp.io <http://shinyapp.io> server. It looks like "myPDF.rnw" can be converted to "myPDF.tex", but there's some issues converting from "myPDF.tex" to "myPDF.pdf".

However, if I simply comment out everything in "myPDF.rnw", making it an empty PDF with only some plane text, I'm able to generate the pdf again on shinyapp.io <http://shinyapp.io>. I'm not sure where the problem is. The main error message I get from the shinyapp log is this:

 "Warning: Error in : Failed to compile makePDF.tex. See makePDF.log for more info.".

It is said in another post that reactive values are not allowed in .Rnw files, but I've seen Yihui's example where he printed two input$*** in the pdf. So I don't think that is the reason.

Any ideas will be more than welcome!

I am considering the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/> professional plan because of the authentication feature. My app will have ~7k users who will access it not much more then 2 times in a year.

Thanks,
Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Shinyapps.io large number of possible users
messages.subject_clean: Shinyapps.io large number of possible users
messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel,

Use the rsconnect::addAuthorizedUser function. I think you can only add one email address at a time, but you can loop over your 7k users easily (maybe add a pause on each iteration so you don't overwhelm the shinyapps API).

The most recent version from Github has an argument emailMessage which will allow you to specify a message to each user. Not sure if that has made it to CRAN yet.

Hope that helps, follow up if not.

-Mason

messages.body_plain:
Currently, we are using the Professional Plan (Monthly) which give us the ability to deploy the website to our own url. I follow the following documentation provided on the shiny official website

https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/custom-domains.html

After following this tutorial, we met two problems. The first one is that we can not get the https certificate for that url. The second problem is that the 'full-screen' button for the leaflet map will not longer work because we get a error like this:

Mixed Content: The page at '<URL>' was loaded over HTTPS, but requested an insecure image '<URL>'. This content should also be served over HTTPS.

Are there some possible solutions for this? Note: We are setting the CNAME using the [blue host] and deploy the application to the shiny web server.

messages.body_plain:
Leo,

Applications served on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> are always served over HTTPS, so you need to ensure that any content in your application including content used by Leaflet is also served over HTTPS.

Also note when using custom domains applications are served in an IFRAME, where the outside frame is NOT served on HTTPS but the application inside the frame is.

Because you are a pro customer, I suggest you open a case with RStudio Support who can help you dig into this more.

-Andy

messages.body_snippet:
Dear all,

I'm struggling with the sadly famous "Unhandled Exception: Repository must be specified for Bioconductor package source" error.

As the deployment fails I have no logs to help the debugging

messages.subject: intermittent 'disconnected from the server'
messages.subject_clean: intermittent 'disconnected from the server'
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I realise this is a question that has been asked alot, but I have looked at the answers and still find no solution. One thing that makes the problem more complicated is that the problem is not reliably there - it only happens sometimes, more often with some customers than others. The problem is:

I have a shiny app which is working perfectly locally. Most of the time, it also works perfectly on the server. However, every now and then, when the first action is performed, the app dicsonnects from the server. I have read suggestions that this could be because the application is too large for my memory application, but on my hard drive, the entire application takes up less than 170MB, and in the admin console, I have set the size to Xlarge (2MB). Playing with the size seems to have little influence on the 'disconnected from the server' error - the error rate at smaller sizes is much the same. In addition, the memory usage in the admin console stays below 300MB.

In the 'user guide', there are many suggestions for things that could be causing the problem, but most of these would cause the error every time the application was run, rather than 5-10% of the time, so I have ruled most of these causes out as well.
We have tried using different browsers (internet explorer, firefox, chrome), and the choice has no impact on the error rate.
I have reduced the 'number of workers per Application Instance to 2', with no effect. The error does not seem to correlate to the number of people using the app at the same time.
Strangely enough, the one thing that seems to help every time is when the customer contacts me to ask about this error. I then try to use the app online (usually with the same error message), after which they can successfully use again.

Any suggestions as to how I can avoid this error would be greatly appreciated.
Thanks

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] intermittent 'disconnected from the server'
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] intermittent 'disconnected from the server'
messages.body_plain:
Have you checked the output from showLogs()?

On Wed, Mar 14, 2018 at 6:14 AM, nm200 <lonz...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> I realise this is a question that has been asked alot, but I have looked at the answers and still find no solution. One thing that makes the problem more complicated is that the problem is not reliably there - it only happens sometimes, more often with some customers than others. The problem is:
>
> I have a shiny app which is working perfectly locally. Most of the time, it also works perfectly on the server. However, every now and then, when the first action is performed, the app dicsonnects from the server. I have read suggestions that this could be because the application is too large for my memory application, but on my hard drive, the entire application takes up less than 170MB, and in the admin console, I have set the size to Xlarge (2MB). Playing with the size seems to have little influence on the 'disconnected from the server' error - the error rate at smaller sizes is much the same. In addition, the memory usage in the admin console stays below 300MB.
>
> In the 'user guide', there are many suggestions for things that could be causing the problem, but most of these would cause the error every time the application was run, rather than 5-10% of the time, so I have ruled most of these causes out as well.
> We have tried using different browsers (internet explorer, firefox, chrome), and the choice has no impact on the error rate.
> I have reduced the 'number of workers per Application Instance to 2', with no effect. The error does not seem to correlate to the number of people using the app at the same time.
> Strangely enough, the one thing that seems to help every time is when the customer contacts me to ask about this error. I then try to use the app online (usually with the same error message), after which they can successfully use again.
>
> Any suggestions as to how I can avoid this error would be greatly appreciated.
> Thanks

messages.subject: does an app need to be redeployed every time the data are changed in order to be real-time updated?
messages.subject_clean: does an app need to be redeployed every time the data are changed in order to be real-time updated?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I recently started using R Shiny and shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> for my job.
Basically, I still have a free shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> account, exploring the options it gives.

I have a question:
Let's say that I've created an app and also deployed it on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
If the data (either they come from a db with values that have been changed in the meanwhile or from a csv file that I have changed) used on the server.R part are changed, do I need to re-deploy the app so that the app on the cloud is updated to the new data?
I mean I don't make any change on the code (which would definitely need a redeployment); I need to update the data used. In fact, the data are very often used for the purpose I need the R Shiny apps, so I would otherwise need to manually redeploy the app often.
If so, do you know a way to automate this re-deployment (since if I put a deployApp() command, I'm asked to press y/n). I've found this https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/236 which I haven't tried yet but should probably be a way (?).

Thank you for any help.

John

Hi Andy,
I include the log below. I don't see anything obvious that would cause the error. There are a few versions that are listed as NA (rmarkdown version, knitr version, etc), but I don't know what affect this would have. The problem seems to occur more in firefox than in internet explorer. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
Cheers,
Nichola

One thing that makes the problem more complicated is that the problem is not reliably there - it only happens sometimes, more often with some customers than others. The problem is:
> > >
> > > I have a shiny app which is working perfectly locally. Most of the time, it also works perfectly on the server. In addition, the memory usage in the admin console stays below 300MB.
> > >

Hello,

I am trying to deploy an App to ShinyApps.io and get the attached error. I understand the error is because of the function "WithSpinner" (part of the Package "shinycssloaders" which shows a loading screen while the result is being fetched ), but i really need the loading screen because it is along running script and it takes some time to execute and bring up the results. Is there something that i need to do to get rid of the attached error? Please advise.

Thanks,
Charan

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] intermittent 'disconnected from the server'
messages.body_plain:
If the user is being disconnected, that is typically because the R process is crashing or exiting for some reason. Any errors should be written to the log. You could consider adding some debug statements to help identify where the application may be crashing.

messages.body_snippet: If the user is being disconnected, that is typically because the R process is crashing or exiting for some reason. Any errors should be written to the log. You could consider adding some debug stateme

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] intermittent 'disconnected from the server'
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] intermittent 'disconnected from the server'
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy,
thanks for the tip. It is not clear to me where I should add debug statements, or what these debugging statements should be looking for, because the problem is not very reproducible, it happens only occasionally and only for some users - otherwise everything runs smoothly. The messages in the log that I thought sounded suspicious are those where a version is listed as NA (see last post for log), but I am not sure how to interpret these messages. Can you tell me what specifically I should be looking for in the debugging, or what these version:NA statements in the log mean?
Thanks,
Nichola

On Friday, 16 March 2018 16:42:17 UTC+1, Andy Kipp wrote:

> If the user is being disconnected, that is typically because the R process is crashing or exiting for some reason. Any errors should be written to the log. You could consider adding some debug statements to help identify where the application may be crashing.

> On Thu, Mar 15, 2018 at 2:50 AM, nm200 <lonz...@gmail.com> wrote:

> >
> > Hi Andy,
> > I include the log below. I don't see anything obvious that would cause the error. There are a few versions that are listed as NA (rmarkdown version, knitr version, etc), but I don't know what affect this would have. There is also a 'browser()' still included, but this is on a tab that is never opened by the user, so I thought it should have no effect. The problem seems to occur more in firefox than in internet explorer. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
> > Cheers,
> > Nichola

messages.subject: How to access username (not user id) to create Log Out button
messages.subject_clean: How to access username (not user id) to create Log Out button
messages.body_plain: I have a private shiny app that will be accessed by multiple users.  I'd like to give them the option to Log Out.  For this I need to dynamically generate a link like https://userName.shinyapps.io/appName/__logout__ <https://username.shinyapps.io/appName/__logout__> however, I'm not sure how to access the current user's userName to do this.  I know I can do session$user, but I believe this provides the user id (e.g. "bgo...@gmail.com") instead of the username (e.g. "ben").

messages.subject: Re: does an app need to be redeployed every time the data are changed in order to be real-time updated?
messages.subject_clean: does an app need to be redeployed every time the data are changed in order to be real-time updated?
messages.body_plain:
If you are bundling your data with your code, then anytime you want to update the data you will need to deploy.
If your code loads the data remotely, then you can create logic to reload the remote data at an interval.

> Hi,
>

> Basically, I still have a free shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> account, exploring the options it gives.
>
> I have a question:
> Let's say that I've created an app and also deployed it on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
> If the data (either they come from a db with values that have been changed in the meanwhile or from a csv file that I have changed) used on the server.R part are changed, do I need to re-deploy the app so that the app on the cloud is updated to the new data?
> I mean I don't make any change on the code (which would definitely need a redeployment); I need to update the data used. In fact, the data are very often used for the purpose I need the R Shiny apps, so I would otherwise need to manually redeploy the app often.
> If so, do you know a way to automate this re-deployment (since if I put a deployApp() command, I'm asked to press y/n). I've found this https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/236 which I haven't tried yet but should probably be a way (?).
>
> Thank you for any help.

messages.subject_clean: Problem to deploy my first shiny app
messages.body_plain:
My apologies, we rolled out a change yesterday intended to make the error one receives when there is an issue with determining Bioconductor packages *more* informative, and ended up making it less so.

The fix for the less informative message should roll out this afternoon.

The underlying problem is that the rsconnect (and its use of packrat) was unable to determine the repository for your Bioconductor packages. We aren't entirely certain the circumstances under which this happens, but typically folks install the latest BiocInstaller and reinstall the Bioconductor packages.
